tagline: Northeast regional bank holding company offering comprehensive commercial, business and retail banking services
hero_kpi_rationale: The most relevant KPI for BBT is the evolution of its total assets, which experienced significant growth following the merger. This reflects the expansion in the size and scope of the company.

kpis.name: Total Assets
kpis.explanation: The total value of everything the company owns.
kpis.description: Total assets doubled following the merger with Brookline Bancorp, Inc., increasing from $11.9 billion to $23.2 billion.

kpis.name: Total Loans and Leases
kpis.explanation: Total amount of loans granted and assets leased by the bank.
kpis.description: Significant increase in loans and leases, primarily driven by assets acquired in the merger.

kpis.name: Total Deposits
kpis.explanation: Total amount of money that customers have deposited in the bank.
kpis.description: Deposits more than doubled, reflecting the integration of deposits from Brookline Bancorp, Inc.

kpis.name: Net Income
kpis.explanation: The company's total profit after all expenses and taxes.
kpis.description: Net income increased by 31.4%, supported by higher net interest income and non-interest income.

kpis.name: Net Interest Margin
kpis.explanation: Difference between interest income earned and interest paid on liabilities.
kpis.description: Net interest margin improved from 3.06% to 3.56%, driven by lower funding costs.

kpis.name: Common Equity Tier 1 Ratio (CET1)
kpis.explanation: Measures a bank's financial strength by comparing its core equity capital to risk-weighted assets.
kpis.description: The CET1 ratio increased, indicating a stronger ability of the bank to absorb potential losses.

kpis.short: Allowance for Loan and Lease Losses to Total Loans
kpis.name: Allowance for Loan and Lease Losses
kpis.explanation: Percentage of loans set aside to cover potential losses.
kpis.description: The allowance for loan and lease losses increased, reflecting prudent risk management in a changing economic environment.

kpis.name: Nonperforming Assets to Total Assets
kpis.explanation: Percentage of the bank's assets that are no longer generating income.
kpis.description: The ratio of nonperforming assets to total assets decreased, indicating an improvement in loan portfolio quality.

kpis.name: Merger of Equals Completion
kpis.explanation: Date on which the merger between Beacon Financial Corporation and Brookline Bancorp, Inc. was finalized.
kpis.description: The merger created a $23 billion entity in the Northeast, combining a stable funding base with a focus on commercial lending.

kpis.short: Commercial Loans to Total Loans Ratio
kpis.name: Commercial Loans to Total Loans Ratio
kpis.explanation: Percentage of total loans that are commercial loans.
kpis.description: The commercial loan portfolio (commercial real estate and commercial and industrial loans) represents 77.4% of total loans, down 6.7 percentage points from 84.1% a year earlier.

risks.title: Interest Rates
risks.score_rationale: The company is sensitive to changes in interest rates, which can impact its net income and financial condition. The language used is intense and the current economic environment is volatile.

risks.title: Competition
risks.score_rationale: The company operates in a highly competitive environment, with both traditional and non-traditional firms. New technologies may intensify competition.

risks.title: Credit Risk
risks.score_rationale: The company faces significant credit risk, particularly in its commercial real estate and commercial loans. Credit losses could have a material impact on the company's results.

risks.title: Inflation
risks.score_rationale: Inflation could negatively affect the company's results and financial condition, especially if interest rates rise.

risks.title: Regulation
risks.score_rationale: The company is subject to strict regulations, which may change and impact its results and financial condition.

risks.title: Liquidity
risks.score_rationale: The company must maintain sufficient liquidity to meet the needs of its depositors and borrowers. Capital market disruptions could affect the company's liquidity.
